constraints.action: Use an end-hole, compliant balloon occlusion catheter for wedged hepatic vein pressure (WHVP) measurements
Inject a small volume of contrast medium when the occlusion balloon is inflated to confirm satisfactory occlusion and exclude hepatic venous-to-venous communications
Use digital, on-screen readings of pressure during WHVP measurement
Record WHVP with a slow speed (up to 7.5 mm/s) in permanent tracings (on paper or electronically)
Stabilize WHVP recording for a minimum of 1 minute, with particular attention to stability during the last 20-30 seconds
Record WHVP in triplicate
Measure free hepatic vein pressure within 2-3 cm of the confluence with the inferior vena cava (IVC)
Measure IVC pressure at the level of the hepatic vein ostium
Use deep sedation during liver haemodynamic measurement
Use light sedation with low-dose midazolam (0.02 mg/kg) if sedation is required
Measure portal pressure gradient (PPG) before and after TIPS insertion
Measure post-TIPS PPG at the main portal vein and at the IVC (at the shunt outflow)
Use immediate post-TIPS PPG measurements to represent long-term PPG values
Measure PPG in haemodynamically stable, non-sedated patients to better reflect post-TIPS PPG values
Achieve a reduction of absolute PPG to <12 mmHg in patients with variceal bleeding undergoing TIPS
Re-measure PPG if there is clinical or Doppler-ultrasonographic suspicion of TIPS dysfunction
Measure HVPG in patients with viral- and alcohol-related cirrhosis to determine the presence of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) when HVPG >−10 mmHg
Measure HVPG in patients with compensated cirrhosis who are not candidates for non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs) and have LSM by TE >−20 kPa or platelet count <−150×10⁹/L to undergo endoscopy
Repeat TE and platelet count annually in patients avoiding screening endoscopy
Repeat LSM every 12 months in patients with cACLD
Perform endoscopy in patients with cACLD and LSM by TE >−20 kPa or platelet count <−150×10⁹/L who are not candidates for NSBBs
Use LSM by TE <−15 kPa plus platelet count >−150×10⁹/L to rule out CSPH in patients with cACLD
Use LSM by TE >−25 kPa to rule in CSPH in patients with virus- and/or alcohol-related or non-obese NASH-related cACLD

Use the ANTICIPATE model to predict CSPH risk in patients with virus- and/or alcohol-related or non-obese NASH-related cACLD with LSM values between 20–25 kPa and platelet count <150×10⁹/L or LSM values between 15–20 kPa and platelet count <110×10⁹/L
Use the ANTICIPATE-NASH model to predict CSPH risk in patients with NASH-related cACLD
Measure spleen stiffness (SSM) by TE in patients with viral hepatitis (untreated HCV or HBV) to rule out and rule in CSPH (SSM <21 kPa and SSM >50 kPa, respectively)
Use SSM <−40 kPa by TE to identify patients at low probability of high-risk varices, allowing avoidance of endoscopy in those not candidates for NSBBs
Measure HVPG in patients with compensated cirrhosis to determine the presence of CSPH when HVPG >−10 mmHg
Measure HVPG in patients with compensated cirrhosis to determine the presence of CSPH when HVPG >5 mmHg indicates sinusoidal portal hypertension
Measure HVPG in patients with chronic liver disease and clinical signs of portal hypertension (e.g., varices, ascites) but with HVPG <10 mmHg to rule out portosinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD)
Measure HVPG in patients with alcohol-related or viral cirrhosis to assess response to non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs)
Measure HVPG in patients undergoing liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to assess presence of CSPH
Measure HVPG in candidates for non-hepatic abdominal surgery to assess risk of short-term mortality if HVPG >−16 mmHg
Measure HVPG in patients with compensated cirrhosis to determine the presence of CSPH when HVPG >−10 mmHg
Measure HVPG in patients with compensated cirrhosis to determine the presence of CSPH when HVPG >5 mmHg indicates sinusoidal portal hypertension
Measure HVPG in patients with chronic liver disease and clinical signs of portal hypertension (e.g., varices, ascites) but with HVPG <10 mmHg to rule out portosinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD)
Measure HVPG in patients with alcohol-related or viral cirrhosis to assess response to non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs)
Measure HVPG in patients undergoing liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to assess presence of CSPH
Measure HVPG in candidates for non-hepatic abdominal surgery to assess risk of short-term mortality if HVPG >−16 mmHg
